title: Who’s Your Judge? On the Detectability of LLM-Generated Judgments

bias_targets.methodology: Extracting text length metrics (e.g., token count, character count, average sentence length) from candidate content and analyzing their feature importance in a trained classifier (J-Detector) to quantify LLM judges' preference for longer responses.

Measuring syntactic complexity using dependency tree depth and average dependency distance, and analyzing its coefficient weight in the detector model to identify LLM preference for complex responses.
Tracking the frequency of discourse markers and hedging expressions to capture LLM judges' preference for confident tones and overconfidence, quantified via feature importance ranking.

Using readability indices (e.g., Coleman-Liau) and lexical diversity metrics to measure the LLM judges' preference for superficially polished and fluent text, evaluated via the detector's feature importance.
